title: China Urban Growth Ratlas (1985–2015)
text:
Between 1985 and 2015, the People's Republic of China underwent the largest physical urbanization process in human history. 
      This ratlas maps the spatial morphology, expansion rings, HOTOSM railway networks, and quantitative growth trajectories across 47 diverse Chinese cities ranked by population.

title: Data & Methodology
text:
1. Primary Data Sources & Scholarly References

A. DLR World Settlement Footprint Evolution (WSF Evolution)

Data Custodian: German Aerospace Center (Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt; DLR), Earth Observation Center (EOC).
Spatial Resolution: 30 meters per pixel, global coverage.
Sensor Inputs: Multi-decadal archive of joint optical (Landsat-5 TM, Landsat-7 ETM+, Landsat-8 OLI) and radar (ERS-1/2, Sentinel-1) satellite observations.
Pixel Encoding: Integer values between 1985 and 2015 represent the exact year of earliest detected settlement establishment. Value 0 denotes unbuilt natural/agricultural surfaces.
Data Access: Retrieved via HTTP range requests through GDAL virtual filesystem (/vsicurl/) from https://download.geoservice.dlr.de/WSF_EVO/.
Primary Scholarly Citation: > Marconcini, M., Metz, A., Üreyen, S., Palacios-Lopez, D., Hanke, W., Bachofer, F., Zeidler, J., Esch, T., Gorelick, N., Kakarla, A., Paganini, M., & Strano, E. (2020). Outlining where humans live, the World Settlement Footprint 2015. Scientific Data, 7(1), 242. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-00580-5
Evolution Methodology Citation: > Marconcini, M., Metz, A., Zeidler, J., & Esch, T. (2021). The World Settlement Footprint Evolution—30 Years of Growth. Remote Sensing of Environment, 255, 112282.



B. HOTOSM Railways of China Dataset

Data Custodian: Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team (HOTOSM) & United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (UN OCHA) Centre for Humanitarian Data.
Platform: Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX).
Data URL: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/hotosm_chn_railways
Content: 433,889 vector railway segments extracted from OpenStreetMap, categorized into passenger-dedicated lines (PDL / 高铁), intercity railways, standard gauge electrified lines, and station coordinates.
Processing: Ingested in R via sf and aggregated into 194 distinct High-Speed Rail corridors (data/processed/hotosm_hsr_lines.rds).
Citation & License: > Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team (HOTOSM). (2024). Railways of China [Data set]. Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX). Licensed under the Open Database License (ODbL 1.0) by OpenStreetMap contributors.



C. ArcGIS Online Big Cities Points Layer

Data Custodian: Esri / ArcGIS Online Feature Services.
Service Endpoint: https://services1.arcgis.com/4TXrdeWh0RyCqPgB/arcgis/rest/services/big_cities_points/FeatureServer
Content: Authoritative geospatial point layer of 184 major Chinese metropolitan centers with national hierarchy ranks (rank 1 to 200).
Role in Ratlas: Validates sample selection, confirms exclusion of tier-1 megacities (#1 Shanghai, #2 Beijing, #3 Guangzhou, #5 Chongqing, #7 Tianjin), and provides an objective national urban hierarchy classification for every city in the atlas.
Citation: > Esri ArcGIS Online. (2023). Big Cities Points Layer [Feature Service]. ArcGIS REST API.



D. Seventh National Population Census of China (七普 2020)

Data Custodian: National Bureau of Statistics of China (中华人民共和国国家统计局; NBS), Beijing, China.
Measurement: Permanent Resident Population (常住人口, Changzhu Renkou) as of midnight, November 1, 2020.
Role in Ratlas: Defines the primary sorting and ranking order across the entire ratlas from #1 Chengdu (20.94 Million) to #47 Hunchun (0.24 Million).
Official Citation: > Office of the Leading Group of the State Council for the Seventh National Population Census. (2021). Major Figures on 2020 Population Census of China. China Statistics Press, Beijing. http://www.stats.gov.cn/



E. GADM Database of Global Administrative Areas

Data Custodian: University of California, Davis (UCD), Department of Environmental Science and Policy.
Version: GADM 4.1 (released 2022).
Data URL: https://gadm.org/
Content: Spatial administrative boundaries at Level 0 (national border), Level 1 (provinces), and Level 2 (prefectures and municipalities) with official bilingual toponyms.
Citation: > Hijmans, R. J., Garcia, N., & Wieczorek, J. (2022). GADM Database of Global Administrative Areas, Version 4.1. University of California, Davis. https://gadm.org/

title: Data & Methodology
text:
3. Four Landmark Urban Development Epochs
Urban expansion in modern China has unfolded in distinct historical waves:

Pre-1985 Core (#F59E0B · Amber Gold): The pre-reform base urban footprint. This includes ancient historical city cores and the industrial settlements constructed during the early Five-Year Plans (1949–1980).
1986–1995 Wave (#EF4444 · Crimson Coral): Deng Xiaoping’s 1992 Southern Tour (Nanxun), the launch of Special Economic Zones (SEZs), and the initial surge of rural-to-urban industrialization.
1996–2005 Wave (#06B6D4 · Electric Cyan): China’s 2001 accession to the World Trade Organization (WTO), the emergence of the “Factory of the World”, highway grid expansion, and initial high-tech development zones.
2006–2015 Wave (#10B981 · Emerald Green): The High-Speed Rail (HSR) construction boom, the Western Development Strategy (Xibu Da Kaifa), massive State-level New Areas (Guojiaji Xinqu), and metropolitan amalgamation.

title: Data & Methodology
text:
4. Quantitative Metrics & Mathematical Definitions

Cumulative Built-Up Area (\(A_t\)): Total surface area in square kilometers occupied by detected settlement pixels up to year \(t\): \[A_t = \sum_{i \in \text{city}} a_i \cdot \mathbb{I}(1985 \le Y_i \le t)\] where \(a_i\) is the ellipsoidal cell surface area computed via terra::cellSize(unit = "km"), and \(Y_i\) is the year of first settlement detection at pixel \(i\).
Net Spatial Expansion (\(\Delta A\)): Absolute urban land footprint expansion between 1985 and 2015: \[\Delta A = A_{2015} - A_{1985} \quad (\text{km}^2)\]
30-Year Growth Multiple (\(M\)): Relative spatial expansion factor: \[M = \frac{A_{2015}}{A_{1985}}\]
Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR): Annualized physical expansion rate over the 30-year observation window: \[\text{CAGR} = \left(\frac{A_{2015}}{A_{1985}}\right)^{1/30} - 1\]
